title: At the Beach
goal: Ask about beach conditions and facilities, arrange an activity, and choose whether to participate.

runs.text: A
lifeguard
supervises water safety at a designated area.
Warning flags
communicate local conditions or restrictions; ask what they mean at that beach. A flag system or another person's assurance should not be turned into a universal guarantee of safe swimming.

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: Is the swimming area open today?

turns.en: Is the swimming area open today?

turns.speaker: Lifeguard

runs.text: Not at the moment. The conditions are rough.

turns.en: Not at the moment. The conditions are rough.

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: What do the flags mean here?

turns.en: What do the flags mean here?

turns.speaker: Lifeguard

runs.text: The posted sign explains them. Today, stay out of the water.

turns.en: The posted sign explains them. Today, stay out of the water.

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: Okay. Where can we check for updates?

turns.en: Okay. Where can we check for updates?

runs.text: At this stand.

This is a fictional local notice. The U.S. National Weather Service describes beach flags as information posted by local beach authorities about current hazards. Ask the lifeguard where swimming is allowed today; flag meanings and marked swimming areas depend on the beach.

study.title: Choose a place and an activity

runs.text: Want to go swimming?

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: Not with the water closed. Let's find some shade instead.

turns.en: Not with the water closed. Let's find some shade instead.

turns.speaker: Friend

runs.text: There's a shady spot by the walkway.

turns.en: There's a shady spot by the walkway.

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: Great. Could we rent beach chairs?

turns.en: Great. Could we rent beach chairs?

blocks.caption: Choose a place and an activity · Friend & Visitor

runs.text: Shade
means shelter from direct sunlight. A
beach chair
is a chair for use at the beach. A
bucket
and
shovel
can be used for sand play. A
beach ball
is a ball used for beach games.
A
surfboard
is a board used to ride waves, usually standing up. A
bodyboard
is a shorter board typically ridden lying down. A
paddleboard
is a board moved with a paddle. A
wetsuit
is a close-fitting suit that helps keep a person warm in water. The surfing and paddleboarding meanings connect with Chapter 72. A
pedal boat
moves by pedaling. If you do not know an activity, ask what it involves rather than equating all equipment.

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: Do you offer beginner surfing lessons?

turns.en: Do you offer beginner surfing lessons?

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: Yes, but today's sessions are canceled.

turns.en: Yes, but today's sessions are canceled.

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: Could we book for another day?

turns.en: Could we book for another day?

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: Tomorrow at ten is an option, subject to conditions.

turns.en: Tomorrow at ten is an option, subject to conditions.

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: Is equipment included, and how long is the lesson?

turns.en: Is equipment included, and how long is the lesson?

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: In this offer, a board and wetsuit are included. It's an hour.

turns.en: In this offer, a board and wetsuit are included. It's an hour.

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: What happens if the conditions are unsuitable tomorrow?

turns.en: What happens if the conditions are unsuitable tomorrow?

runs.text: I'll explain our cancellation arrangements.

blocks.caption: Ask about lessons or rentals · Visitor & Employee

runs.text: Ask “Do you have a wetsuit in a child's size?” “How much is the rental?” or “When does it need to be returned?” Prices, requirements, and availability are particular to the operator.
You may say “I'm excited to try it,” “I'd rather watch today,” or “That's outside my comfort level.” Your decision does not need to copy a friend's enthusiasm.

Fictional beach card: swimming closed now; updates at the lifeguard stand; beach-chair rental available; today's lessons canceled; possible beginner lesson tomorrow at ten, one hour, board and wetsuit included; cancellation terms not yet explained.
Ask about swimming and the flags. Partner uses the card. Tell a companion your alternative plan.
Ask about tomorrow's lesson, equipment, and cancellation terms. Partner gives known details and offers to explain the missing condition.
Decline the activity or accept only after asking your question. Use your own comfort level or a role.
Solo: speak both roles, then hide your visitor turns and respond to the employee prompts. Later change the activity to a paddleboard rental and ask for its own conditions.
Possibilities:

“Let's stay on the beach today.” “Is the wetsuit included?” “I'd rather watch this time.” Check that the condition, question, and choice are clear. No water-safety skill or real rental is being tested.
Source note: [National Weather Service beach-flag context](https://www.weather.gov/safety/ripcurrent-faqs).
